items.title: Mixed Signals: Weight-Space Programming for EEG and ECG
items.summary: Weight-space programming allows language models to read a trained neural network's weights and edit them. This opens the door to ``training'' by reasoning rather than through gradient descent. Prior work has demonstrated its functionality and promise for game-playing networks and fixing specific failures in language models, even extending to diffusion models. In this work, we present its applicability to models trained on biosignal data, specifically EEG and ECG data. items.title: Module-Aware Optimization for Graph Neural Networks
items.summary: Different optimizers impose different geometries on parameter updates. Adaptive methods such as Adam and AdamW use coordinate-wise updates, while matrix-aware optimizers such as Muon utilize weight-matrix structure through orthogonalized updates. For Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), however, the effective geometry of its weight matrices is shaped not only by its learned channel-mixing weights, but also by the graph-propagated representations it acts on. items.title: Read Less, Solve More: Token-Efficient Sparse Reading of External Content for AI Agents
items.summary: Web-facing AI agents repeatedly access webpages, documents, repositories, and tool responses, yet reading interfaces often expose entire objects when only sparse evidence is needed. This over-reading increases token and latency costs and can dilute relevant evidence. We present SparseRead, a reusable reading control layer that governs content admission without modifying the agent model. Its Read Intent Protocol tracks evolving needs and source coverage; Adaptive Reader Backends select how evidence is located and exposed; and the Budgeted Read Gate bounds cumulative raw exposure per episode wit…

items.title: Interactive Visual Gym: Evaluating Visual Interaction Models with Simulated Users in Interactive Worlds
items.summary: Visual interaction models that support users during ongoing physical tasks require evaluation in closed loop, where assistant responses can change subsequent user behavior and task outcomes. Existing benchmarks largely rely on offline replay and therefore cannot capture these effects. We introduce Interactive Visual Gym, a framework for closed-loop evaluation and training of visual interaction models through joint simulation of executable task environments and human users. We contribute three simulators that recreate everyday tasks and human-aligned action spaces across cooking, household mani…

items.title: Scaling Mathematical Proof Supervision from Structured Textbooks
items.summary: Mathematical supervision for language models is typically flattened into isolated problem-solution pairs, discarding the curricular organization and evidential structure of the original sources. We introduce TOME-Math (Textbook-Oriented Mathematical Evidence), a large-scale corpus that converts 2,118 textbooks spanning the core areas of university-level mathematics subjects into approximately 380K structured proof-supervision records while preserving chapter order, proposition-proof links, dependency references, and source provenance. Leveraging these structural signals, we explore curriculum …

items.title: CogBattery: Human-Referenced Evaluation of Cognitive Task Behavior and Structure in Language Models
items.summary: Human cognitive tasks let us compare language models with humans under controlled conditions. Yet a model can reproduce the direction of a human effect while making different errors. CogBattery evaluates 54 open-weight language models on text adaptations of 13 cognitive paradigms, comparing each with human data from its source study. Like humans, models respond more to n-back lures than to controls, yet they make far more false alarms on ordinary non-targets. Most models' reported confidence separates correct from incorrect answers less well than humans' does, and most always choose the same w…

items.title: WMIP: A Working-Memory-Inspired Programmable Probe of Cumulative State Tracking in Large Language Models
items.summary: Human working memory lets people maintain and update information. Large language models (LLMs) face a related demand when tracking updates within a single prompt without writing out intermediate states, yet existing tests differ in their constraints on written steps. We introduce a working-memory-inspired probe of cumulative state tracking with program-computed answers, 3 to 100 updates, and final-state, intermediate-state, or multi-target queries. It compares protocols on identical items. Across 18 LLMs, accuracy is 84.9% on single-step arithmetic but 31.7% on core items requiring one number …

items.title: Ensemble Routing for Prompt-Adaptive Cost-Aware LLM Inference
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly support Web-based services that must balance response quality and inference cost across heterogeneous requests. Conventional routing selects one model per prompt, while fixed ensembles cannot adapt their composition and cost to individual requests. We introduce PISA, a prompt-adaptive, cost-aware single-model router, and PISA-E, its extension to ensemble routing. At the core of both methods, PISA combines soft cluster memberships with model-specific predictors to estimate individual model capabilities. Building on these estimates, PISA-E jointly select…

items.title: Incentivizing Self-Learning in Large Language Models via Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) draw on parametric knowledge and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to solve knowledge-intensive tasks. Yet problem solving in unfamiliar domains calls for tightly coupled knowledge acquisition and reasoning, beyond factual retrieval and aggregation or learning solely from a preassembled context. We study self-learning -- autonomously retrieving, studying, and applying knowledge from long-form reference materials on the fly. To investigate this capability, we formulate a textbook-based mathematical problem-solving task. LLMs must navigate textbook exposition, lea…

items.title: GTAGym: Real AAA Game Tasks Environment for Evaluation and Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: AAA games offer a rich testbed for evaluating agent perception, reasoning, and control. However, evaluating whether agents can complete tasks in AAA games is challenging and often human-annotated because task outcomes are often difficult to verify automatically, let alone applying it for Reinforcement Learning (RL). We introduce GTAGym, an environment and framework for evaluation and RL on GTA V tasks. Its evaluation benchmark, GTAVBench, derived from GTA V main-story missions, contains 103 online tasks reconstructed across nine task families, alongside 47 image-based shooting and sniping task…

items.title: LO-World: Unified BEV Latent Modeling for Joint 4D Occupancy and LiDAR Forecasting
items.summary: LiDAR point clouds and 3D semantic occupancy represent two distinct modalities capturing fine-grained metric geometry and dense volumetric semantics, respectively, holding natural potential for mutual complementarity. However, existing world models typically forecast these modalities independently or cascade them heuristically, missing the opportunity for reciprocal cross-modal regularization. To address this, we propose LO-World, a unified 4D world model that forecasts both modalities within a shared BEV latent space. items.title: One Table, Many Queries: Benchmarking Generalist Tabular Models Across Generation, Imputation, and Prediction
items.summary: Generation, imputation, and prediction query different aspects of the same tabular distribution, but are usually evaluated separately. This leaves unclear which capabilities they share, how their training objectives interact, and whether one model can perform all three well. We introduce the One Table Benchmark (), spanning 56 datasets, 46 registered methods, and 20 capability axes under aligned data splits and explicit task contracts. items.title: Visual Similarity in Adult Word Extension and Artificial Word Learning
items.summary: When two objects share a name, how much does their visual similarity explain, and what do the teaching examples add? First, we reanalyzed trial-level data from a large adult word-extension study (Lewis & Frank, 2018), computing each test image's distance to the examples shown in the space of a frozen self-supervised visual encoder (DINOv2). items.title: Prompt2Echo (P2Echo): Text-Prompted Multi-View Echocardiography Segmentation with One Model
items.summary: Automated segmentation in multi-view echocardiography is essential for comprehensive cardiac assessment, yet remains challenging due to substantial anatomical and appearance variability across standard acoustic windows. In this paper, we present P2Echo, a unified framework capable of segmenting diverse cardiac structures across multiple standard echocardiographic views using a single model controlled by structured view-aware text prompts. items.title: Test-Time Scaling for Diffusion Language Models with Frequency-Aware Remasking
items.summary: Diffusion language models (DLMs) generate text through iterative denoising, where decisions about which tokens to commit or remask strongly affect output quality. Existing certainty-aware strategies rely on instantaneous confidence or entropy, but these local signals can be misleading on difficult reasoning problems. We formulate DLM test-time scaling as adaptive allocation of both inference compute and decoding strategies. Our two-stage approach uses a fast base sampler to solve easy questions, then applies frequency-aware remasking to the remaining hard questions. This strategy tracks how of…

items.title: Embodied First Exam
items.summary: Early successes on agentic robotics point to a potential paradigm shift toward using coding agents to control robots. Existing robotics benchmarks are built around visuomotor policy learning, leaving it open whether coding agents can reliably control diverse robots under physical-world constraints. We therefore introduce the Embodied First Exam, a unified, comprehensive, and agent-native evaluation framework where coding agents can choose their own control approach: direct control, code to control, or train a policy to control. items.title: LEASH: Stay Safe in Agentic Robotics
items.summary: Foundation models such as GPT and Claude have shown strong capabilities in spatial understanding and embodied intelligence. These advances make agentic robotics a promising path toward artificial general intelligence in robotics. However, we find that using foundation models to control robots poses serious safety risks, and comprehensive safety evaluation is still lacking. We introduce RoboRisk, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating safety in agentic robotics. items.title: PhyRubric: Rubric-Grounded Diagnostic Evaluation of Physical Commonsense in Text-to-Video Generation
items.summary: As text-to-video (T2V) models are increasingly positioned as world simulators, it is essential to evaluate whether their videos conform to physical commonsense. However, existing benchmarks rely on annotators who rate each video with a single score based on intuition, yielding ratings that are subjective and do not tell which physical principle is violated. We introduce PhyRubric, a rubric-grounded diagnostic framework for evaluating physical commonsense in T2V generation. items.title: DyCraft: An Agentic System for Long-Horizon 4D Scene Generation
items.summary: While frontier coding agents can generate high-quality 3D scenes and articulated assets, they struggle to create coherent long-horizon animations. When equipped with general-purpose harnesses, they frequently produce physically implausible outputs, generating objects that interpenetrate, lack physical support, or move unnaturally. Such bare agents struggle to repair these errors because they default to scripting the full animation in one pass, making it difficult to verify their work and disentangle complex spatiotemporal constraints. items.summary: A scientific agent can give the same verdict while reading and citing different evidence. BioAgent-DF tests this separation using paired reference and candidate values saved at the same scientific computation site. It restores or transplants those values at their original coordinates, then runs the agent on healthy hardware. items.title: TorchCurves: Differentiable Parametric Curves
items.summary: We present TorchCurves, a PyTorch library that treats vector-valued parametric curves as learnable primitives. Its central operation maps batches of scalar inputs to points on curves represented in B-spline or Legendre polynomial bases, with differentiation through both inputs and coefficients. items.title: The Surprising Effectiveness of Deleting Weights in LLM Post-Training
items.summary: How little of a pretrained large language model (LLM) has to change for it to acquire new capabilities? We find that zeroing fewer than 0.05% of its weights, with no other modification, matches full fine-tuning (FFT) at scale across three LLM post-training regimes: reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, supervised fine-tuning, and on-policy distillation. items.title: Micius-Flash: Lightweight Agentic Intelligence for Engineering
items.summary: We introduce Micius-Flash, a 27-billion-parameter model for engineering with native multimodal input, deep reasoning and a 256K-token context window. We design the Micius data pipeline as a knowledge-tree-driven data flywheel comprising three stages: knowledge tree construction and expansion, data synthesis, and quality validation with hard-example augmentation. items.title: MACaQ: Fast, Model Agnostic Calibrated Quantization for Low-Precision Weights and Activations
items.summary: Weight-activation quantization can reduce the memory and compute cost of neural-network inference, but recent methods often require expensive optimization and architecture-specific propagation of basis transforms across layers. We introduce MACaQ, an MXFP4 W4A4 post-training quantization method that treats every linear layer independently. items.title: Medical Image Segmentation: Foundation Model Adaptation versus Task-Specific Training
items.summary: Foundation models pretrained on large natural-image collections are increasingly adapted for medical image segmentation, in the expectation that they will replace models trained for each task. items.summary: DeepLearning (DL)-based Computer-Aided Diagnostic (CAD) systems have shown great promise in supporting clinicians, but their performance heavily depends on the availability of large, well-annotated datasets. items.title: AutoScaffold: AI-Guided Scaffolding for Reinforcement Learning of Language Models
items.summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) produces rich training experience, yet outcome rewards reduce each attempt to a single number and leave most of this information unused. Training-time scaffolds, such as strategies or hints added to the prompt during training, offer a natural way to turn this information into guidance, but their design and adaptation are largely left to humans and tailored to specific domains. items.title: Contrastive Discovery: Open-Ended Scientific Discovery over Competing Explanations
items.summary: LLM agents are increasingly used for open-ended, data-driven scientific discovery, yet most of them evaluate hypotheses pointwise, testing an empirical claim $h$ only against its complement $\neg h$. When evidence rejects $h$, the agent learns that one explanation is unlikely but not which alternative the evidence supports. items.title: Pyrite: Building and Benchmarking Protein-Ligand Pose Ranking Agents
items.summary: Predicting how a ligand binds to its target is central to small-molecule drug discovery. Modern cofolding models can generate diverse candidate poses, but reliably ranking these candidates remains challenging. We introduce Pyrite, a pairwise pose-ranking benchmark comprising 1,500 pose pairs across diverse protein-ligand complexes. Expert chemists equipped with 3D visualization tools and physics-based scores perform near chance, highlighting the difficulty of interpreting available chemical signals. items.summary: Connectome-constrained models are often used to argue that a measured wiring diagram outperforms shuffled or rewired wiring, and hence that structure shapes function. items.summary: Agent harnesses have emerged as a promising mechanism for continual learning, alongside test-time parametric learning. However, the current benchmarks have several limitations: they generally focus on a single applied domain, serve each instance only once, and assume a single family of learner, so memory-based and weight-based systems are rarely compared on the same scale. items.summary: Foundation models trained on large unlabeled corpora develop emergent capabilities, tasks that go beyond the training objective. We extend this paradigm to multimodal biology with Bonbon, a foundation model for molecular interactions trained on approximately 3.2 trillion tokens of paired protein-ligand sequences. items.summary: Biological visual systems compute reliably under tight metabolic and wiring constraints, whereas artificial vision systems consume far more energy and can be sensitive to adversarial perturbations. items.summary: Cross-sensor remote sensing image retrieval aims to find scenes with the same content across heterogeneous sensors, such as SAR and optical or panchromatic (PAN) and multispectral (MS) imagery, without manual labels. items.summary: Deploying LLM-based analytics agents in enterprise settings requires evaluation frameworks that can reliably detect failures across complex, multi-tool workflows. items.summary: Business process automation runs the same Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) again and again on new inputs. Large Language Model (LLM) agents can follow an SOP written in natural language, but they call an LLM to choose every step of every run, which adds latency and cost at scale. items.summary: Research ideation is iterative: researchers refine their ideas step by step based on feedback. items.summary: 一个美食创作者想把镜头从餐桌全景慢慢推到一碗面上。这个动作不难，难的是他没有第二个人帮他推，也没有空间在桌上架一条滑轨。最后他切了一个固定机位，画面清楚，但缺少呼吸感。 这张桌子，是今天很多内容创作的真实现场。产品测评、美食、美妆、直播、带货，大量拍摄都发生在几平方米之内。 设备其实已经不差：手机能拍4K，口袋云台能稳住画面，相机的画质早已溢出大多数人的需求。可一旦镜头需要“动起来”，需要推、拉、环绕、升降，普通人手里那套东西就接不上了。 相机已经够好了，但运镜依然是一门需要多年训练的手艺。越千创新做的，就是把它变成一台机器能执行的动作。 创始人曾诚在剧组待过，硕士阶段研究的是机器人轨迹优化。公司2023年成立，最早做面向剧组的大型摄影机器人，后来一路减重，把技术路线切换到五公斤级的桌面产品。 支撑这次切换的，是对专用场景下恒定负载的精准理解：相机作为末端负载重量恒定，调平之后重力被平衡，电机要做的不是举起相机，而是让相机动起来，由此衍生出了零重力直驱技术，也作为产品轻量化的基础。结合全自由度和AI导演决策，构成了越千创新的产品路径——第一代服务专业创作者，第二代走向消费级，或将进入大疆、影石所在的价格带。 影像行业正走到一个需要新答案的节点。参数竞争的天花板已经出现，便携体验也做到了接近极限，下一段竞争不再停留在“拍得清楚”，而在于帮用户把想拍的内容真正完成。 一家三十人的创业公…

items.summary: 11月11日，蚂蚁集团旗下个人AI助理灵光公布最新数据：自10月27日灵光2.0上线以来，累计托管事务量突破300万项，累计执行任务超过1100万次。 这是灵光2.0上线以来又一次披露事务托管数据。11月5日，灵光曾公布，上线一周已托管超过116万项事务，累计执行任务超过360万次，用户规模突破2000万。 与用户规模、对话次数等传统AI产品指标不同，事务托管量衡量的是用户有多少件事交由AI持续跟进。其增长反映出，个人AI助理的使用方式正在从即时问答、单次任务执行，向长期事务管理延伸。 这一变化的关键，是AI从响应指令转向持续履约。传统AI助手通常在用户发起问题或指令后完成一次交互。而灵光2.0推出的“帮我管”功能，允许用户在授权后，将需要长期关注的事务交给AI，由其持续监测状态，并在满足条件或到达关键节点时主动提醒、执行相应操作。 例如，家长可以让灵光持续关注钉钉班级群，汇总重要通知和待办事项；消费者可以托管机票价格变化监测、会员自动续费提醒；用户还可以通过连接智能家居设备，让AI根据预设条件自动执行操作。这些场景的共同点是：任务并不在一次对话中结束，而是需要AI在用户不持续介入的情况下，保持关注并适时采取行动。 支撑这一能力的，是长期任务调度、跨会话上下文管理及外部服务连接能力。截至11月3日，灵光已接入支付宝、钉钉、夸克、飞书等40余项外部连接器，将AI的服务范围扩展至工作、…

items.title: 夹缝中生存的中国程序员
items.summary: 大龄程序员，正身处一个前所未有的窒息夹缝之中。 在国内，背负着沉重的房贷与全家的开销，却要面对“优化线”的残酷现实。十几年的开发经验不再是护城河，反而成了公司眼中的高昂人力成本，每天都活在随时可能被边缘化甚至被淘汰的焦虑里。 为了不被时代抛弃，好不容易折腾起“梯子”连上外网，想借助全球最顶尖的 AI 工具重塑自己的竞争力。可迎面撞上的，却是更冰冷的技术封锁与制裁。从 Claude 严苛的环境风控，到 OpenAI 无预警的大规模封号，甚至连每月咬牙花 200 美元订阅的账号也随时可能瞬间清零。网络限制、支付壁垒、物理位置判定，层层关卡把这帮人死死挡在技术前沿的门外。 每天下班后，还要像打游击一样折腾节点、换账号，提心吊胆地防止被封。只不过是想用最先进的工具写好代码、体面地养家糊口，究竟做错了什么，才要在这个时代承受如此荒诞的双重夹击？

items.summary: 各位老哥大家好，今天我是兴高采烈啊。我是大专，26 年毕业了来深漂。 来的时候配置狠狠拉跨，那个时候支付宝欠了几千块钱，随后又问朋友借了 3000 块钱。手里除了这-3000 没有任何现钱。 4 月 9 日，我找到一个工作，结果那个工作带上老板带上我总共 3~4 个人。写代码的，干了两周就跑路了。 当时住在青旅里面，一天 50 元。青旅大家知道的，总会遇到有意思的人，老板给我价格减到 43 。这样我手头的钱总算能坚持到发工资了。那个时候我心里还很忐忑：这个工作室太小了，有点像是发不出来工资的呀。索性工资顺利到账。让我又苟了两个星期，那个时候我也抑郁发作，天天想 si 算了，在青旅爬起来买了舍曲林吃吃。继续投工作，总算又找到了一个工作。 实习 5000 ，不签劳动合同，不转正。后来 leader 看我技术还可以，给我提到了 6000.先干着呗，干了四个月，公司发奖金。我技术尚可，原 CTFer 转开发，leader 可能怕我走，给我申请了 20k 奖金。至此，这四个月入 12k/月。每个月还会存钱的。在拿了奖金以后，工资提升到了 9.1k 下半场正在做，昨天老师让我申请了奖学金 10k 。是挑战杯团队赛，我们学校给 10k 奖金。我负责的项目，有电子开心。等奖学金发下来，我就铺完了我的资金垫子：30k ，到时候足够半年多无工作 GAP 了。如果遭遇意外被裁我终于不担心了。 自 4 月…

items.title: 不知道的迷信，它生效吗？
items.summary: 预告：我知道这可能是一个比较具有争议性的问题，我先说明，我很叛逆。 --- 这篇文章始于一个问题：一个月前外公走了，两个月后我能参加好友的婚礼吗？ 我的观点是，**只要我不告诉对方，我开心地去参加，那毫无问题**。我跟另一个人讨论这个问题，他表示强烈反对：对方有知情权，有的人就很在意，你不说就会影响到人家，你就是素质低。 我首先就问了，我不说，到底怎么影响到别人？对方说问就是玄学。但是这里面确实有一个值得玩味的问题。 **如果对方不知道，这个迷信成立吗？** 对于一些近乎疯狂的“玄学爱好者”，他们会觉得不行，不行的！会有感应的！你这人去到那了对人家就不好了！不管别人知不知道！他就是不好。嗯，我真的没什么好说，也不想反驳，我又不能证伪，怎么反驳。 ## 说与不说的结果 想一想，说的结果无非两种。 一是拒绝，二是没问题，可以来。我觉得现在唯物主义的 90 后应该会比较少说不能来，毕竟两件事并不是贴得很近。但是如果真的觉得我不能去，那不去就可以了，尊重对方的想法。 如果他说没问题呢，对我来说结果是可以去，但是有可能对对方来说却可能承受了一次扩散膈应，这个下面再说。 如果不说呢？**实际上 0 人受伤**。没有人会感觉的膈应，没有人受到诅咒，一切正常。 **除非对方是一个能感应到我外公走了的灵能者，还顺便觉得最近有点生活不顺，并归因为这是我的锅**。 所以实际上，选择说与不说，至少是没有一…
